subject.title: [Feature]: Subagent session reuse for expert agents (avoid new session per spawn)

question: Should native `sessions_spawn` gain a core opt-in reuse/pooling API, should Microsoft Teams gain a conversation-binding adapter for thread-bound spawned sessions, or should native subagents remain isolated with reuse limited to ACP/thread-bound paths?
rationale: The missing source path is clear, but the permanent answer changes session-state semantics, tool/API surface, concurrency behavior, cleanup, and channel ownership boundaries; automation should not choose those product rules.

options.title: Design Core Native Reuse
options.body: Add an explicit, scoped native reuse contract after defining TTL/liveness, locking, cleanup, and history-isolation rules.

options.title: Add Teams Binding First
options.body: Implement Microsoft Teams through the channel conversation-binding adapter seam and leave ordinary native `mode="run"` isolated.

options.title: Keep Native Runs Isolated
options.body: Document ACP resume and thread-bound sessions as the supported reuse paths and close native run reuse as out of scope.

recommendation.title: Design Core Native Reuse
recommendation.body: Add an explicit, scoped native reuse contract after defining TTL/liveness, locking, cleanup, and history-isolation rules.

likelyOwner.reason: This is the strongest available routing candidate across the central native subagent spawn path and the broader session-state/API boundary.
